root.summary: row, grid, band — the three containers docs/design/layout-language.md adds. This page is itself an example of all three, plus a sections[] section proving the two spines coexist.

nodes.title: row, grid, band
nodes.tagline: One tree, all three containers, plus a sections[] section — coexisting on one page.

sections.name: Why this exists
sections.summary: std-doc shipped exactly one content column in every layout and forced every doc through node -> sections -> numbered cards. This page is the counter-example.

content.text: A row column is a block, or a bare array of blocks — no wrapper object. This lead band's own label appears in the "on this page" aside ABOVE the sections[] entry, because adaptNode hoists at:"lead" blocks before the section spine.

cols.text: This column is a bare array of two blocks.
Both render in one .row-col, with no wrapper — the single riskiest claim in the design, proven here and in go/internal/core/layout_language_test.go.

cols.body: This column is a single block — also legal, no array required.

content.text: grid auto-flows a FLAT list of blocks — no per-cell wrapper, because auto-flow means the author is explicitly not choosing placement.
band > row > grid > panel — four levels deep, still renders every leaf and every leaf's CSS.
